name: page-ceiling
description:
A landscape whose scroll never ends: every page hands back an @odata.nextLink, none of them ever repeats, and no @odata.count is reported. That is the shape the walk has no answer for -- it is driven by the next link alone, so it used to spin until the task timed out with nothing in the log. The repeated-link check cannot help here because each link is new, which is exactly why the page ceiling exists behind it. MAX_PAGES stops the walk at 500 pages and prints the truncation, which is what log_contains pins.

The 501st scripted response carries no next link. It exists ONLY as a terminator for a regression: a scroll that never ends would otherwise fail this scenario by timing out rather than by failing an assertion, and with it an uncapped walk stops one request later and fails on request_count and the missing log line instead.

Page one carries a real device so the scenario still proves rows are parsed and reported; every later page carries a record with neither DiscoveryId nor DeviceID, which build_assets skips -- that is what keeps the ids unique across 499 pages.

check_determinism is off: the scenario already costs 500 requests, and a second identical run would only re-assert an id paged already pins.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in paged: the id is the bare Ivanti DiscoveryId with no tenant scope.

log_contains: ivanti-neurons: stopped at the 500 page ceiling with 500 devices collected
